//: Claude Code project settings.json — place in .claude/settings.json at repo root. Comparable permission scoping should be configured wherever Antigravity or another agent tool exposes it (check the tool's own permission/allowlist settings — the principle transfers even if the config format doesn't).

permissions.//: Deny list wins over allow list. The goal: the agent can freely edit implementation code, but touching the files that DEFINE correctness always requires explicit human action outside the agent session.

//comment_on_ask: Files under 'ask' aren't blocked outright — an agent legitimately needs to write new tests. 'ask' forces an explicit approval prompt each time rather than a silent edit, so a test-weakening change can't slip through inside a larger multi-file commit without you seeing it happen.
//comment_on_deny: Files under 'deny' are things an agent should never touch as part of 'fixing' a failing check — if the pipeline itself, its config, or an already-accepted golden file needs to change, that's a deliberate human action taken outside the agent's autonomous loop, not something the agent decides to do to make a red pipeline turn green.
